# ARCHITECTURE

This is the short architecture signpost for the docs surface.

Bijou is a nine-package monorepo for terminal software in TypeScript. The root
[ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is the main entrypoint, but DOGFOOD and
the docs lane still need a repo-owned summary here.

## Structure

- `@flyingrobots/bijou` owns the pure core: prompts, themes, components, and
  surfaces
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` owns the fullscreen runtime, layout, motion,
  overlays, and framed shell
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-node` owns the terminal/process boundary, worker
  runtime, and recorder
- the i18n packages own runtime catalogs plus localization authoring/exchange
  workflows

## Read Next

- [root architecture signpost](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [runtime architecture](../packages/bijou-tui/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [node architecture](../packages/bijou-node/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [core architecture](../packages/bijou/ARCHITECTURE.md)

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

All packages (`@flyingrobots/bijou`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-node`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui-app`, `create-bijou-tui-app`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-i18n`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-i18n-tools`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-i18n-tools-node`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-i18n-tools-xlsx`, `@flyingrobots/bijou-mcp`) are versioned in lock-step.

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Four DOGFOOD modules no longer read Node files: `app-ids.ts` and
  `app-prompt-font.ts` import their JSON, and the landing logo and the
  translated guides are generated JSON copies (`examples/docs/generated/`,
  written by `npm run components:data`, held to their files by
  `tests/dogfood-browser-data.test.ts`). Terminal output is unchanged.
- DOGFOOD reads its Markdown documents through one seam,
  `examples/_shared/documents.ts` (the live file, then the verified corpus,
  as before). The web GPU showcase's build resolves it to a browser adapter
  that serves a generated table of exactly the documents the app reads, so
  `examples/docs/app.ts` reaches no Node API.

### Added

- The web GPU showcase mounts DOGFOOD, the documentation app: `?app=dogfood`
  on the showcase page, and `/dogfood.html`, a page with no chrome whose
  Surface fills the window and resizes with it. The app and its document table
  load on demand, so the page's entry chunk does not carry them. The browser's
  language picks DOGFOOD's locale, and the choice stays in the page.
- The web GPU showcase can present one app on either host and keep its state.
  A Host switch beside the backend switch (`Space` then `m`) stops the canvas
  mount and starts `mountBijouDom()` with the same model, and back again. The
  new dual-host counter example has both projections; apps with no scene
  projection keep the DOM choice disabled and say why (flyingrobots/bijou#869).

- The `bijou-tui` raytrace vector helpers (`raytraceAdd`, `raytraceSub`,
  `raytraceScale`, `raytraceCross`, `raytraceNormalize`, `raytraceReflect`)
  accept an optional `target` of the new `RaytraceVector3Mutable` type. The
  result is written into it and returned, so CPU-bound loops allocate nothing
  per call; the target may alias any input, and results equal the allocating
  form bit for bit. Calls without a target are unchanged (#348).
- Regression tests prove East Asian wide-character layout in `wrapToWidth()`,
  `constrain()` truncation and `table()` in `interactive` and `static` modes,
  for Han, kana, halfwidth katakana, precomposed Hangul, fullwidth forms and
  emoji between ideographs, with a property test over widths 2..120. The
  narrow East Asian Ambiguous policy is now stated and pinned. The reference is
  `docs/topics/text-width/`. The tests found five defects, filed as #851,
  #852, #853, #854 and #855 (#678).

- `npm run code-dojo:cycles` holds the repository's runtime import cycles to a
  checked-in inventory, `scripts/code-dojo/baselines/runtime-scc.json`: the
  strongly connected components of the runtime import graph, built from
  TypeScript's syntax tree with type-only imports and re-exports left out. A
  new, grown or merged component, or a new edge inside one, fails; a component
  that shrinks or disappears fails as stale until `npm run
  code-dojo:cycles:write` records it. The check is a step of `code-dojo:verify`
  and `code-dojo:ci`. Today's inventory holds 16 components and 49 modules.
  Output is JSON Lines with schemas in `schemas/` (#638).

- `npm run code-dojo:report` writes the Code Dojo debt aggregate, next goalpost
  target, per-source counts, top ESLint rules and optional live ESLint data to
  `docs/code-dojo/debt-report.json` as a `code-dojo.debt-report.v1` document,
  with `--check` for drift and `--live-input`/`--out` for a live artifact. The
  numbers come from the same `summarizeCodeDojoDebt()` the `code-dojo:debt`
  gate uses, which is unchanged. JSON Schemas are in `schemas/` (#603).
- `npm run code-dojo:live` runs the ESLint ratchet's own analysis and writes a
  `code-dojo.eslint-live.v1` file (default `.cache/code-dojo/eslint-live.json`)
  for `code-dojo:report --live-input`. It prints one JSON Lines event with the
  stored ESLint ceiling, the live count, the signed slack and the next legal
  ceiling (`--human` for prose, `--schema` and `--help` for the contract). The
  total uses `summarizeEslintResults`, the function `lint:eslint` uses. It is
  not wired into CI, hooks or any gate, and no baseline or verdict changed
  (#369).

### Fixed

- The sealed runner's local launchers (`scripts/docker-seal/run.mjs` and
  `bootstrap.mjs`) no longer wrap each run in `git locks with`, so `npm test`,
  `npm run soak` and every other local command run on a machine without
  `git-locks`. A second concurrent local run is refused at once with a message
  saying another run holds the worker; callers that want queueing wrap their
  own command (flyingrobots/bijou#865).

- `mountBijouCanvas()` paints the last frame again after a container resize
  that leaves the grid unchanged. Resizing the presenter clears the canvas, and
  with no change of columns or rows the app rendered nothing, so the canvas
  stayed blank until the next key (flyingrobots/bijou#867).

- `npm run dogfood:i18n:debt` prints each logical surface once. The inventory's
  per-surface rows are now aggregated from the entries by surface through
  `aggregateDogfoodI18nDebtSurfaces()`, so a surface split across part files
  (`counter-block-demo`, `release-title`, `storybook-app`) is no longer repeated
  once per file. Totals, per-surface counts and baselines are unchanged (#490).

- The Windows sealed runner's toolchain context measurement no longer fails
  when a running step removes a directory after the walk listed it and before
  it was read. Such a directory now counts as empty; a missing root or any
  other error (`ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`) still fails, and the entry and byte limits
  are unchanged. This is the Windows counterpart of the Linux supervisor fix
  (flyingrobots/bijou#820) and does not address the Windows storage allowance
  (flyingrobots/bijou#788) (flyingrobots/bijou#826).

- The Theme Lab draft theme keeps its rule provenance. `cloneThemeForThemeLabEditor()`
  no longer hand-copies each token family: it copies through
  `renameRuleAuthoredTheme()`, so a field added to `Theme` later is carried
  and `ruleAuthoredDefinitions(draft)` returns the base theme's definitions.
  The "Why this value" panel now inspects the draft being edited rather than
  the unedited base, and reset restores value and provenance together (#503).

- `scripts/record-gifs.ts` settles each VHS job exactly once. A spawn `error`
  followed by `close` no longer appends a second result or counts a second
  completion; the first outcome wins and spawn failures are still reported.
- `npm run audit:components` no longer measures a backdrop that
  `compositeSurface()` dimmed under an overlay as unreadable text. The
  compositor records, internally and without a new export or Surface field,
  the rectangles its overlays covered; a cell outside them that still carries
  the compositor's `dim` is skipped by the contrast check. Text an overlay
  draws, dim or not, and dim text drawn without a dimming compositor are still
  measured. The baseline shrinks from 48 to 32 errors: the 16 `modal/*`
  entries were each its 158-cell dimmed backdrop (#581).

### Added

- `breadcrumb()` mirrors under right-to-left layout (#615). With
  `direction: 'rtl'` or an `rtl` context, `interactive` and `static` output
  reads right to left, keeps the current item (the last logical one) styled,
  and mirrors a directional separator glyph (`›` to `‹`). ASCII separators,
  labels, paths and IDs are never changed, and `pipe` and `accessible` output
  keep logical order. `ltr` output is unchanged. The Component Library heading
  uses it instead of drawing the trail by hand.

- `progressBar()` mirrors under right-to-left layout (#619). It takes
  `direction` (or reads `ctx.direction`); in `interactive` and `static` output
  the fill grows from the right edge, the gradient's leading edge is the
  rightmost cell and the percentage label moves to the right of the bar. Fill
  stays whole cells, so there is no partial-block glyph to mirror; caller fill
  glyphs go through `mirrorGlyphs()`. `pipe` and `accessible` output and every
  left-to-right render are unchanged.

- `box()`, `headerBox()`, `boxSurface()` and `headerBoxSurface()` align the
  border title to the logical start edge of the resolved direction: the right
  edge under `rtl` in `interactive` and `static` modes. `ltr`, `pipe` and
  `accessible` output is byte-identical to before; title text is never
  reversed (flyingrobots/bijou#626).

- The Components Library's `r` toggle now reaches every story preview.
  `createStoryProfileContext()` in `examples/_stories/protocol.ts` takes an
  optional `direction`, and the library passes `ltr` or `rtl` from the toggle,
  so a component that reads `ctx.direction` through `mirrorsLayout()` mirrors
  in `interactive` and `static` previews and keeps logical order in `pipe` and
  `accessible`. A story's own `direction` option still wins. At `ltr` every
  existing frame is unchanged, and no story file gains copy
  (flyingrobots/bijou#840).

- CI publishes a per-job wall-time summary to the run's job summary, slowest
  finished job first, with skipped, in-progress and cancelled jobs labelled.
  The new `Wall time summary` job is read-only, non-blocking and required by
  no other job (flyingrobots/bijou#609).

- A regression test builds a temporary repository with several unpublished
  commits and runs the pre-push hook's own `changed_paths_for_push` and
  `is_dogfood_relevant_path` against a first publication (all-zero remote
  object id), asserting paths from every commit are detected, a branch with
  unrelated files stays non-relevant, and an existing remote branch diffs
  against the remote object (#552).

- `stepper()` and `paginator()` mirror under right-to-left layout (#617). With
  `direction: 'rtl'` or an `rtl` context, `interactive` and `static` output
  runs the steps and page dots right to left: the first step or page is
  rightmost and the logically next one sits to its left. Step markers, labels,
  step numbers, the `──` connector and the `Page X of Y` text are never
  reversed or altered, and neither component emits a directional glyph, so no
  glyph mapping applies. `pipe` and `accessible` output keep logical order.
  `ltr` output is unchanged.

### Added

- `ui-scene-ir/1` nodes can declare an optional `state.checked` boolean,
  validated by `validateUiSceneIr()` (`invalid-node-state`). The browser seam
  lowers it as `data-bijou-checked`, and `mountBijouDom()` writes
  `role="switch"` and `aria-checked` for a `switch` node, patched in place. A
  scene that declares no state keeps its canonical bytes and hash. The parity
  witness records the state as a `browser-only-fact` gap (#807).

### Added

- The web GPU showcase mounts the Components library and the hero app, and
  its browser suite switches `counter -> components -> hero` and toggles the
  three ten times. Both apps now import in a browser: their fonts, DOGFOOD
  catalogs, example snippets and design-system families are imported instead
  of read from disk at module load (the snippets and families as generated
  JSON, kept current by `npm run components:data` and a drift test), and the
  hero perf overlay reads memory through a port with a Node and a browser
  adapter. Their terminal output is unchanged (#809).

- `tree()`, `enumeratedList()` and `accordion()` mirror under right-to-left
  layout (flyingrobots/bijou#622). With `direction: 'rtl'` (a new option on
  each, as on `breadcrumb()`) or an `rtl` context, `interactive` and `static`
  output indents from the right: tree connectors mirror by explicit mapping
  (`├` to `┤`, `└` to `┘`), list markers keep their text and sit on the right
  edge, and the accordion disclosure glyph follows the title (`▶` to `◀`; `▼`
  is not directional). Lines are padded to the widest line by display width, so
  no width option exists. Labels, paths and IDs are never changed, `pipe` and
  `accessible` output keep logical order, and `ltr` output is unchanged.

### Changed

- The DOGFOOD docs SVG path parser (`examples/docs/svg-path.ts`) is total and
  no longer loops forever on a number after `Z` (for example
  `M0 0 L1 0 L1 1 Z 2 2`). Malformed input now throws
  `SVG path: ... at offset N.`: a number after `Z`, a command with too few
  numbers, and any unsupported character (lowercase commands, exponents,
  unsupported command letters), which were previously dropped or reinterpreted
  under the previous command. Valid uppercase `M`, `L`, `Q`, `Z` paths render
  unchanged (#473).

- DOGFOOD story documentation shows canonical family Content guidance and
  Ownership, matching the Components Library while preserving the story's own
  summary and usage advice (#586).
- The `guidedFlow()` story's docs, variant label, and preview copy resolve
  through the DOGFOOD catalogs in `en`, `fr`, `es`, and `de`. Stories can opt in
  through a `localize` hook, documented in `docs/development.md`.

### Fixed

- `runScript()` records each frame as a snapshot of the screen at that update.
  A framed app, DOGFOOD among them, repaints one reused Surface, and every
  entry of `frames` was that one Surface, so every entry showed the last frame
  and a test reading an earlier frame or searching all frames saw only the
  final screen. A Surface view is now copied once per recorded frame, with
  `Surface.clone()`; the frame passed to `onFrame` is the same snapshot, and
  `testRuntime()` snapshot frames get the same fix. `recordDemoGif()` GIFs no
  longer repeat the final frame for such apps. The result's shape is unchanged
  (flyingrobots/bijou#822).
- `npm run version` rejects versions with leading-zero numbers such as
  `01.0.0` and `1.0.0-rc.01` before it edits any manifest or runs npm, using
  the same canonical integer rule as release preflight. Stable and
  `-(rc|beta|alpha).N` versions behave as before
  (flyingrobots/bijou#553).
- A sealed Linux run no longer fails with exit status 2 when a test removes a
  temporary directory while the supervisor is measuring generated bytes. The
  supervisor's walk of `/tmp` could see a directory such as a fixture
  repository's `.git/refs/tags` and then find it gone before reading it
  (`ENOENT ... scandir`). A directory that vanishes after it was listed now
  counts as empty; a missing root or any other error still fails the run, now
  with a message saying the supervisor's measurement failed, not a test
  (flyingrobots/bijou#820).
- DOGFOOD's "Language set to ..." notice now appears in the language just
  chosen in settings, not the one being left: choosing Spanish from French
  shows "Idioma establecido en español / Español." The notice is localized
  with the target locale's catalogs, including any `extraI18nCatalogs`
  (flyingrobots/bijou#582).
- The DOGFOOD locale ratchet's language-cycle cases no longer time out on hosted
  runners. Each rendered 79 settings-toast ticks, each a full page render, and
  took 10 to 15 s hosted against a 15 s limit. They now use a scripted clock
  that lets the toast expire in two ticks (`tests/helpers/scripted-compressed-time.ts`),
  and take about 4 to 5 s per file hosted. No assertion changed; a new case pins
  that the compressed run ends on the same frame as real-time ticking (#778).
- The DOGFOOD touched-file rule compares a touched split lineage, such as a
  story helper of `examples/docs/stories.ts`, against the whole lineage at the
  base. It had read only the changed files at the base, so every raw string of
  their unchanged siblings was reported as added copy (#809).
- The web GPU showcase's page chrome, on both its pages, is now a Vite + React
  app built only from shadcn components installed from the `@flyingrobots`
  registry, with a theme-book light, dark and system theme that persists, big
  type, a layout from phone width to extra-wide, Skeleton and Spinner loading,
  GSAP motion, and vim-style keys with `Kbd` hints (`Esc` opens a command
  palette). While focus is in a Bijou mount every key goes to the app, and
  chrome styles never reach the canvas or the `mountBijouDom()` elements; the
  counter's frame digest is unchanged on all three backends (#815).
- The web GPU showcase is pinned to Geordi `52ba6bb`, which ships its
  procedural glyph table (flyingrobots/geordi#205) and pins the canonical WGSL
  digest inside the WebGPU presenter (flyingrobots/geordi#189). The vendored
  `procedural-glyphs.json`, its digest check and its `proceduralTable` argument
  are gone. The counter's frame digest is unchanged on all three backends; the
  Canvas 2D receipt's `executedArtifactSha256` changes, because the package now
  hashes `createCanvas2DSurfacePresenterCore` (#810).
- A click on a canvas mounted by `mountBijouCanvas()` now leaves keyboard focus
  in its hidden textarea. Chrome's `mousedown` default action moved focus off
  the canvas after the `pointerdown` handler had focused the textarea, so no
  key reached the app; the mount now focuses the textarea again on
  `pointerup`. The web GPU showcase's browser suite found it (#797).
- `lowerUiSceneToSurface()` resolves a token color only from an own entry of
  `tokenColors`, as `lowerUiSceneToBrowser()` does. A token named
  `constructor`, or a `tokenColors` object that inherits entries, no longer
  colors a cell. The parity witness found the difference (#443).

### Removed

- DOGFOOD no longer ships the unrendered `release-story-current*.md` sources that
  described v7.2 as current. The Current Release Story renders
  `release-story-active*.md`, and its tests assert that source (#585).

### Added

- DOGFOOD docs pages have a contextual drawer (#627). `i` opens it and moves
  focus into it; `Esc` or `i` closes it and returns focus to the pane that had
  focus, or to the page's content pane if a resize has hidden that pane. The
  drawer is a layout pane in all four layout variants, not an Overlay, so it
  never dims the frame. It is closed by default and closes on page change.
  `bijou-tui` adds a `context-drawer` frame layer directly above `workspace`.
  A page declares it through `layers()` with the drawer `paneId`, and the
  frame puts it in the layer stack only while that pane has focus.
- The DOGFOOD Components reading path shows the active variant, its position
  and the variant count, and the active profile inline in the story pane
  (#624), at every layout width and in all four locales. The facts no longer
  depend on the wide-only variants pane, so the contextual drawer migration can
  remove that pane without removing a required fact.
- Framed apps reuse the focused-pane scroll measurement across consecutive
  scroll actions (#589, DL-032). Each runtime owns one single-entry cache keyed
  by a frame input revision, page, pane, columns and rows. Any message other
  than a scroll action invalidates it, as does initializing the app again.
  The measurement Surface is no longer module-global. Scroll behaviour is unchanged.
- Components can resolve a layout direction (#612). `BijouNodeOptions` and
  `BijouContext` gain `direction?: 'ltr' | 'rtl'`, and `createBijou()` and
  `createTestContext()` accept it. `resolveDirection()` lets the explicit
  option override the context and defaults to `'ltr'`; `mirrorsLayout()`
  keeps `pipe` and `accessible` output in logical order. `directionalSide()`,
  `orderForDirection()`, `mirrorGlyph()` and `mirrorGlyphs()` map logical
  edges, sequences and directional glyphs (‹ ›, ▸ ◂, → ←) for right-to-left
  layout. No Component mirrors yet; the family tasks under #573 adopt it.
- Design record DL-029 decides the DOGFOOD Code Dojo debt dashboard: a
  `release` page guide that renders a committed `code-dojo.debt-report.v1`
  snapshot and an append-only `code-dojo.debt-history.v1` ledger, with no live
  computation at render time (#601). The proposed contracts keep report checks
  optional, distinguish unavailable live data, and preserve cited history with
  idempotent recording and explicit unknown or zero-debt goalpost states.

- Design record DL-036 decides which book edition to translate first: the
  teaching book (about 13,600 lexical tokens). Planned translations will live
  in `bijou-job-monitor` under `book/locales/<locale>/` and build to per-locale
  PDFs after #618. The English
  hash pins do not change. Each language's translation splits into two tasks
  of about 4.5 hours (#616).
- DL-038 decides the Wesley boundary (#663). Bijou pins `wesley-cli`
  exactly to `0.3.0-alpha.3` and spawns the CLI at build time over its
  `--json` output. Core gets a pure emitter over Wesley L1 IR. A missing or
  mismatched Wesley is a hard error with no fallback parser.
- `examples/web-gpu`, a Vite page that mounts the counter and the component
  showcase with `mountBijouCanvas()` on Geordi's WebGPU, WebGL2 and Canvas 2D
  presenters, with a HUD of backend, fallback reasons, grid, cell size, device
  pixel ratio, frame time and receipt evidence, and controls for backend
  switching, WebGL2 context loss and atlas reset (#797). Geordi's packages are
  vendored as tarballs pinned to one commit and installed offline. A
  Playwright suite, `npm run test:browser:web-gpu`, drives the page in Google
  Chrome; it is the one test lane outside the sealed runner. The build refuses
  every Node.js built-in, so `examples/components` and `examples/hero`, which
  read files at module load, are listed as refused rather than mounted.
- `mountBijouCanvas()` takes an app factory, called once with the run's
  context, and a `css` option passed to the run (#797).
- The browser suite also checks `mountBijouDom()` in Google Chrome on
  `examples/web-gpu/dom.html`: one dispatch per click, Enter and Space on a
  `<button>`, and an `<input>` that keeps its element, focus and selection
  through typing and an IME commit (#797).
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-web` has `mountBijouDom()` (#796). It runs a
  `SemanticSceneApp` in a DOM container as native elements: a `button` or
  `switch` role becomes a `<button>`, and a `textbox` becomes an `<input>`.
  Each scene is lowered with `lowerUiSceneToBrowser()` and patched in place,
  keyed by `data-bijou-node-id`, so an input keeps its element, value, and
  selection across re-renders. Delegated `click`, `keydown`, `input`, and
  composition events become action requests; a native button activates once.
  Focus that loses its node moves to a declared node, an ancestor, or the
  root. Theme tokens are `--bijou-semantic-*`, `--bijou-surface-*`, and
  `--bijou-border-*` custom properties that update live, and `dir` follows
  the model. `stop()` removes every listener and stops the app. The tests use
  an in-memory document; no browser runs them. Reference:
  `docs/topics/bijou-web-dom/README.md`.
- `mountBijouCanvas()` in `@flyingrobots/bijou-web` runs a TEA app on a
  `<canvas>` it owns inside a container (#795). Presenters are injected per
  backend through a structural `BijouCanvasPresenter` interface that Geordi's
  presenters satisfy, so the package does not depend on Geordi. `'auto'` tries
  `webgpu`, `webgl2`, then `canvas2d`, each on a fresh canvas, records
  `fallbackReasons`, and falls back only on unavailability; a renderer fault
  or a forced backend's unavailability rejects. Frames coalesce onto
  `requestAnimationFrame`; the container's device-pixel box and DPR set the
  grid; a zero-size container defers the mount. `switchBackend()` swaps canvas
  and presenter while the run, model, focus and input stay; `stop()` is
  idempotent and leaves nothing attached. `createWebInteractiveContext()`
  composes a context around `createWebInteractiveIO()`. The package now has
  `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` as a peer dependency. Tested with in-memory fakes
  only, not in a real browser.
- `createWebInteractiveIO()` in `@flyingrobots/bijou-web` reads browser input
  through a hidden `<textarea>` and a surface element (#793): keys, IME
  composition (delivered once in either `compositionend` and `input` order),
  single-line paste (multi-line paste is rejected), pointer and wheel with
  0-based cells and SGR packets on `rawInput()`, a platform-aware shortcut
  pass-through, and idempotent `dispose()`. It uses structural DOM interfaces
  and has not run in a real browser.
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` has a semantic scene app contract (#794).
  `SemanticSceneApp` is an `App` that also projects its model to a
  `ui-scene-ir/1` scene and maps a declared action to a message.
  `createSemanticSceneController()` validates each scene, dispatches only
  action ids that the current scene declares, and sends each message through
  the `EventBus` to `update()`. An undeclared or removed action id gives a
  typed diagnostic and no state change. Listeners get each frame once, in
  commit order, also when a listener invokes an action. The terminal runtime
  is unchanged. Reference: `docs/topics/semantic-scene-app/README.md`.
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-web` is a new workspace package for browser hosts
  (#792). `createWebContext()` composes `createWebClock()`,
  `createWebRuntime()`, `createWebStyle()`, and `createWebOutputIO()` into a
  `BijouContext` for all four output modes, with no runtime dependencies and
  no Node.js imports. Output goes to caller-supplied sinks or in-memory
  buffers. `readFile`, `readDir`, `question`, and `rawInput` refuse with a
  typed `WebUnsupportedCapabilityError`. The package is not published to npm.
- `SurfacePresenter` is a synchronous host seam in `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`
  for hosts that are not terminals (#791). Pass one to `run()` as
  `RunOptions.presenter`. In `interactive` mode the runtime then calls
  `enter?()`, `present(current, target, ctx)`, `onResize?(cols, rows)`, and
  `exit?()`, and writes no frame, screen, cursor, or mouse bytes to `ctx.io`.
  A run without a presenter is unchanged. The `static`, `pipe`, and
  `accessible` output modes ignore the presenter. The contract does not cover a
  hardware cursor overlay, OSC 8 hyperlinks, or a window title.
- `@flyingrobots/bijou` has a browser renderer seam for `ui-scene-ir/1`
  (#442). `lowerUiSceneToBrowser()` lowers a scene with a `geordi-browser`
  target profile to a deterministic element tree and HTML markup that hold only
  scene facts. `createUiSceneBrowserDom()` builds the tree through a host
  document, and `createUiSceneBrowserReceipt()` fills `outputs.browser` in a
  `ui-scene-receipt/1`. The terminal renderer is unchanged. Reference:
  `docs/topics/ui-scene-browser/README.md`.
- `@flyingrobots/bijou` has a terminal and browser parity witness for

  shell interpolation failures.

  inventory page now resolves its title, summary, body copy, headings, and
  detail labels/descriptions through the DOGFOOD string table and generated
  runtime catalogs instead of accepting new raw visible English into the i18n
  debt baseline.

  paints landing background, logo, wordmark, and panel cells with explicit
  Bijou-owned backgrounds, so custom terminal-profile background colors do not
  leak through the landing renderer.
- **AppFrame foreground ownership** — Frame-rendered panes now apply the
  paired surface foreground when they paint a Bijou-owned background behind
  unstyled cells, so DOGFOOD and other framed apps do not inherit unreadable
  terminal-profile foreground colors after users customize their terminal
  theme.
- **Localization loader activation staging** — Loader-backed locale activation
  now stages third-party catalog bundles and rebuilds the candidate entry table
  before swapping loader catalogs or committing locale/direction changes, so a
  conflicting catalog bundle cannot leave the runtime half-switched.
- **Localized array payload validation** — `freezeLocalizedValue()` now applies
  the same portable boundary checks to array-owned properties as plain objects,
  rejecting symbol, non-enumerable, accessor, named, and self-referential
  non-index properties instead of silently dropping them while cloning indexed
  array items.
- **DOGFOOD locale page labels** — Framed page tab, layer, palette, and search
  labels can now resolve from the active page model instead of being snapped at
  app construction, and no-loader locale switches commit synchronously so
  DOGFOOD language cycling refreshes visible shell labels in the next frame
  without ignored asynchronous locale work.
- **DOGFOOD locale catalog overrides** — Language cycling now reloads
  caller-provided extra i18n catalogs after generated DOGFOOD catalogs, so
  host and test catalog overrides survive selected-locale changes.
- **Atomic locale switching** — Loader-backed `setLocale()` now commits locale,
  direction, and loader-managed catalogs only after the selected locale catalogs
  load successfully, so failed locale switches leave the runtime on its previous
  locale state.
- **Localization resource immutability** — `I18nRuntime.resource()` now returns
  cloned, deeply frozen resource values through the same portable localized
  value boundary used by `localize()`, so callers cannot mutate catalog-backed
  runtime state by retaining resource objects or arrays.
- **Localization value boundary validation** — `freezeLocalizedValue()` now
  enforces the documented portable catalog boundary with deterministic errors
  for cyclic graphs, symbol-keyed properties, non-enumerable properties,
  accessors, class instances, functions, symbols, and bigint values instead of
  silently dropping metadata, shallow-freezing mutable objects, or overflowing
  the stack.
- **Block render node cycle rejection** — `blockRenderNode()` now rejects cyclic
  plain slot/config records with deterministic contract errors while preserving
  existing snapshot behavior for inert plain data.
- **DOGFOOD localization failure visibility** — DOGFOOD text lookup no longer
  catches every localization-port failure and falls back to English copy, so
  unexpected adapter/catalog failures remain observable instead of being hidden
  behind fallback text.
- **Counter fixture terminal width** — The DOGFOOD `CounterDemoBlock` fixture
  now sizes its preview card with ANSI-aware grapheme width so styled progress
  bar output does not inflate the card width.
- **Localization runtime method binding** — `I18nRuntime.t()` now resolves
  messages through closure-owned runtime state so callers can destructure or
  pass the helper as a function without losing access to localization state.
- **Nested block visual composition** — Standard block visual rendering now
  preserves child `Surface` output as surface-native content instead of
  flattening nested block output to plain text and recreating cells without
  styling.
- **Block render node snapshots** — `blockRenderNode()` now snapshots plain
  slot/config records at construction time, so mutating caller-owned input
  objects after node creation no longer changes later render output.
- **DOGFOOD block preview readability** — Selected block preview pages now keep
  raw compact metadata summaries, source paths, and embedded preview scrollbars
  out of the live TUI documentation surface. The overview stays an index of
  available blocks and stories, while selected block pages show a live example,
  clipped lowering preview, and concise human-readable block documentation.
- **Standard block TUI rendering** — First-party standard blocks now return
  surface-backed output in interactive and static modes while preserving text
  output for pipe and accessible modes, so DOGFOOD can display the actual block
  render result instead of a hand-written preview mock.
- **DOGFOOD Blocks preview rendering** — The Blocks preview now composes live
  block example `Surface`s directly instead of flattening them into accordion
  text before render, preserving TUI styling and bordered example surfaces.
- **Spring example API drift** — `examples/spring` no longer passes the removed
  `fps` option to `animate()`, keeping the interactive spring comparison aligned
  with the current pulse-driven animation command API.
- **Stable spring animation under slow pulses** — `animate()` spring commands
  now integrate with bounded fixed timesteps instead of applying large runtime
  pulse deltas directly to spring physics. Slow terminal frames may delay spring
  progress, but they no longer turn one delayed pulse into a large position or

  values across sampled subpixels instead of borrowing the first lit
  subpixel's style. Empty Braille cells can now retain averaged background
  color, so shader-authored procedural images no longer need app-local
  post-render color correction loops.

## [4.3.0] - 2026-04-10

### ⚡ Performance

- **RE-008 byte-packed surface representation** — the internal `Surface` data structure is now backed by a packed `Uint8Array` (10 bytes per cell) instead of an array of heap-allocated `Cell` objects. Colors are stored as raw RGB bytes, modifiers as a flags bitfield, and characters as uint16 code points with a side table for multi-codepoint graphemes. The differ compares cells via 10-byte equality checks instead of string comparison, and emits ANSI SGR escape sequences directly from buffer bytes with a cached style lookup — bypassing chalk entirely on the hot diff path. Surface composition (`blit`) copies bytes directly between packed buffers. `fill()` and `clear()` use a template-stamp approach. A new `setRGB()` API writes numeric RGB values directly into the buffer with zero string parsing or object allocation. All components have been migrated to use `setRGB` when the surface is packed, with Cell-based fallbacks preserved. See the [RE-008 design doc](book/bijou-designs.pdf#page=1426) for full details.
- **RE-017 byte-pipeline performance recovery** — full recovery of the render pipeline to pre-RE-008 performance and beyond. The diff path is now **32% faster on dense gradient frames** and **64% faster on sparse updates** vs the pre-cycle baseline. Key optimizations:
  - **Theme token color cache** — `Cell.fgRGB` / `Cell.bgRGB` fields let components skip per-cell hex parsing when theme tokens already carry pre-parsed RGB. The `tokenToCellStyle` helper threads them automatically for `createTextSurface` consumers. 1.9× paint speedup on synthetic theme-heavy surfaces.
  - **Render-dirty bitmap** — a second `Uint32Array` on `PackedSurface` tracks which cells were painted since the last `clear()`. The differ scans the bitmap union (target | current) word-at-a-time and skips cells that weren't touched in either surface. Unchanged frames return in near-zero time (**30× faster** on diff-static). Sparse updates (~10% dirty) are **1.9× faster**.
  - **Byte-native differ** — `renderDiffPacked` writes cursor moves, SGR prefixes, and cell characters as raw UTF-8 bytes directly into a pooled `Uint8Array` and hands them to `WritePort.writeBytes()` in one shot. No per-frame string concatenation, no `sgrCache` Map, no `String.fromCharCode` key allocation. The TUI runtime allocates the pooled buffer alongside the framebuffers and resizes it on terminal resize.
  - **Bench v2** — process-isolated, wall-time-only, scenario-agnostic benchmark harness (`bench/` workspace package) with 9 scenarios covering paint, diff, and realistic multi-region composition. CoVs <5% across all scenarios. See [bench/README.md](../bench/README.md).
  - Full audit and running log in [docs/perf/RE-017-byte-pipeline.md](book/bijou-designs.pdf#page=1843).

### ✨ Features

- **`Surface.setRGB()` zero-allocation API** — new method for hot rendering paths that writes character code + numeric RGB directly into the packed buffer. Roughly 10–50x faster than `set()` for per-cell writes. The `set()` API is preserved with documentation noting it parses hex strings on every call.
- **`PackedSurface` interface** — extends `Surface` with `.buffer` (the raw `Uint8Array`), `.sideTable` (grapheme cluster lookup), `.markAllDirty()`, `.markAllRenderClean()`, and `.renderDirtyWords` for buffer-copy and dirty-tracking workflows. Exported from the main barrel.
- **`TokenValue.fgRGB` / `TokenValue.bgRGB`** — theme tokens now carry pre-parsed numeric RGB channels alongside hex strings, populated automatically at theme resolution time.
- **`WritePort.writeBytes(buf, len)`** — optional method for byte-level output. Node's `process.stdout.write(buf)` adapter implements it; the packed differ uses it to bypass string encoding on the hot path.
- **`RenderState.outBuf`** — the TUI runtime's rendering pipeline now carries a pooled byte buffer through all stages, available to the Diff middleware for direct byte emission.
- **Modifier flag constants** — `FLAG_BOLD`, `FLAG_DIM`, `FLAG_STRIKETHROUGH`, `FLAG_INVERSE`, `UNDERLINE_SOLID`, etc. exported from the main barrel for `setRGB` flag arguments.
- **`@flyingrobots/bijou/perf` subpath export** — public access to packed-cell utilities (`parseHex`, `encodeModifiers`, flag constants) for performance-sensitive consumer code.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **RE-016 modifier-dropping in setRGB fast paths** — `setRGB` calls in `canvas.ts`, `overlay.ts`, `focus-area.ts`, and `notification.ts` now pass `encodeModifiers(cell.modifiers)` instead of omitting the flags argument. Previously the Cell-based fallback preserved bold/dim/strikethrough/etc. but the packed fast path silently dropped them.
- **RE-015 braille art corruption resolved** — `flexSurface` with `align: 'center'` no longer corrupts braille characters (U+2800–U+28FF). The packed byte-copy blit preserves all character codes directly without intermediate string processing. Verified with a 420×140 (58,800 cell) braille art test case — zero mismatches.

## [1.2.0] — 2026-03-04

### ✨ Features

- **Vim-style mode switching for `filter()`** — interactive filter starts in normal mode where `j`/`k` navigate. Any printable character (except `j`/`k`) enters insert mode and types the character. Press `/` to enter insert mode without typing. `Escape` in insert returns to normal; `Escape` in normal cancels. Mode indicator shows `:` (normal) or `/` (insert).

### 🐛 Fixed

- **`k` key asymmetry in `filter()`** — `k` always navigated (even when query was non-empty), preventing users from typing `k` as a search character. Now properly handled via normal/insert mode switching.
- **`clearRender()` consistency in `filter()`** — navigation handlers now capture `renderLineCount()` before mutating state, preventing visual artifacts when the filtered list shrinks.
- **`filter()` viewport scrolling** — the filter list viewport was locked to `slice(0, maxVisible)`, so the cursor indicator disappeared once the user navigated past the visible window. Now tracks a `scrollOffset` that slides to keep the cursor in view.
- **Markdown code spans not isolated** — code span content (backtick-delimited) was vulnerable to subsequent bold/italic regex passes. For example, `` `a*b*c` `` in pipe mode became `abc` instead of `a*b*c`. Now uses NUL-delimited placeholders to isolate code span content.
- **`textarea()` empty submit ignores defaultValue** — submitting an empty textarea with Ctrl+D returned `''` instead of falling back to `defaultValue` when set.
- **`markdown()` width not validated** — negative or NaN width values flowed unchecked into `String.repeat()` in the separator renderer, causing a `RangeError`. Now clamped to a minimum of 1.
- **`markdown()` HR regex misses spaced variants** — `* * *` and `- - -` are valid CommonMark horizontal rules but were mis-parsed as bullet list items because the bullet regex matched first. HR regex changed from `/^(-{3,}|\*{3,}|_{3,})\s*$/` to `/^([-*_]\s*){3,}$/` on trimmed input.
- **DAG `cellAt()` CJK column mapping** — CJK/wide characters occupy 2 terminal columns but 1 grapheme slot, causing garbled rendering when `cellAt()` indexed directly by column offset. Now builds a column-to-grapheme mapping via `expandToColumns()` during `PlacedNode` construction.
- **Numbered list continuation indent misalignment** — continuation lines of wrapped numbered list items used per-item prefix width, causing misalignment between items 1–9 and 10+. Now calculates max prefix width across all items and uses it uniformly.
- **DAG `Math.max(...spread)` overflow** — `Math.max(...nodes.map(...))` in `renderInteractiveLayout()` could throw `RangeError` for arrays > ~65K elements. Replaced with `reduce()` loop.
- **DAG accessible edge count mismatch** — `renderAccessible()` header counted all declared edges but rendered only edges with existing targets, causing the "Graph: N nodes, M edges" summary to disagree with the body. Now counts only valid edges.
- **`textarea()` cleanup summary ignores defaultValue** — submitting an empty textarea with Ctrl+D showed "(cancelled)" in the summary line instead of the resolved `defaultValue`. Refactored `cleanup()` to accept the resolved value and cancelled flag.
- **`textarea()` maxLength=0 ignored** — truthy checks (`options.maxLength && ...`) treated `0` as unset, allowing unlimited input. Changed to nullish checks (`options.maxLength != null`).
- **DAG duplicate node ID misdiagnosed as cycle** — `assignLayers()` reported "cycle detected" when given duplicate node IDs. Now validates uniqueness before topological sort with a clear "duplicate node id" error message.
- **`junctionChar()` empty set returned `┼`** — an empty direction set (no edge traffic) now returns `' '` (space) instead of a four-way junction character.
- **Unnecessary type casts and redundant code** — remove `as 'interactive'` cast in static-mode test, narrow `linkReplacer` param type to `string` (removing `as string` cast), remove redundant null-equality clause in DAG token run-length encoding, return `renderInteractiveLayout()` result directly instead of destructuring into a new object.
- **`filter()` cursor flicker** — move `hideCursor()` from `render()` (called on every repaint) to one-time setup before the event loop.
- **Asterisk HR assertion** — strengthen `***` horizontal rule test to assert box-drawing character instead of non-empty output.

### ♻️ Refactors

- **Split `dag.ts` (941→~200 lines)** — extract edge routing into `dag-edges.ts`, layout algorithms into `dag-layout.ts`, and renderers into `dag-render.ts`. `dag.ts` remains the public facade with types and entry points.
- **Split `markdown.ts` (468→~50 lines)** — extract block/inline parsers and word wrapping into `markdown-parse.ts`, block renderer into `markdown-render.ts`. `markdown.ts` remains the public facade.
- **Extract `textarea-editor.ts`** — move the ~192-line interactive editor state machine from `textarea.ts` into a dedicated module. `textarea.ts` remains the public facade.
- **Extract `filter-interactive.ts`** — move the ~152-line interactive filter UI from `filter.ts` into a dedicated module. `filter.ts` remains the public facade.
- **`encodeArrowPos()` / `decodeArrowPos()`** — replace `GRID_COL_MULTIPLIER` arithmetic with self-documenting bitwise encoding functions `(row << 16) | col`, supporting up to 65535 rows/cols.
- **Shader-based DAG edge rendering** — replace pre-allocated `charGrid`/`tokenGrid` arrays in `renderInteractiveLayout()` with on-demand `cellAt()` per-cell computation using a spatial node index and highlight cell set.
- **Simplify `j` key handling in `filter-interactive`** — in insert mode, `j` falls through to the printable handler instead of being special-cased in the down-arrow condition block.
- **DRY `parseInlinePlain`/`parseInlineAccessible`** — extract shared `parseInlineStripped()` function; the two variants differed only in link replacement format.
- **Textarea running counter** — replace O(n) `lines.join('\n').length` recomputation on every keystroke with a maintained `totalLength` counter updated on insert/delete/newline.
- **Textarea dynamic line-number gutter** — replace hardcoded `prefixWidth = 6` with dynamic calculation based on line count, preventing overflow at 1000+ lines.

- **Keybinding manager** — `createKeyMap()` for declarative key binding with modifier support (`ctrl+c`, `alt+x`, `shift+tab`), named groups, runtime enable/disable, and `handle(keyMsg)` dispatch.
- **Help generator** — `helpView()` (grouped multi-line), `helpShort()` (single-line summary), `helpFor()` (filter by group prefix). Auto-generated from registered keybindings.
- **Input stack** — `createInputStack()` for layered input dispatch. Push/pop handlers (KeyMap or any `InputHandler`), dispatch top-down with opaque (modal) or passthrough (global shortcuts) layers.

### Changed

#### Core (`@flyingrobots/bijou`)

- **`IOPort` interface** — added `onResize()` method (breaking for custom port implementations)

#### TUI runtime (`@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`)

- **`Cmd` type signature** — Now `(emit: (msg: M) => void) => Promise<M | QuitSignal | void>`.
- **`App.update()`** signature now receives `KeyMsg | ResizeMsg | M` (was `KeyMsg | M`)
- **TEA runtime** refactored to use `EventBus` internally — single subscription drives the update cycle

### Fixed

#### TUI runtime (`@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`)

- **Layout height rounding** — `renderColumn` now correctly pads to the full target height, ensuring footers are anchored to the bottom row.
- **Row cross-axis alignment** — `flex()` row direction no longer conflates inline text alignment with cross-axis (vertical) alignment. `align: 'end'` correctly positions content at the bottom without right-aligning text.
- **Flicker-free rendering** — Refactored `renderFrame` to use `join('\n')` and `\x1b[K` (clear-to-end-of-line), preventing unwanted terminal scrolling and top-line clipping.
- **Scroll-safe initialization** — `enterScreen` now disables auto-wrap (`\x1b[?7l`) to ensure writing to the bottom-right corner doesn't trigger a scroll.
- **Layout hardening** — `flex()` and `hstack()` are now resilient to zero or negative dimensions (preventing `RangeError: repeat count must be non-negative`).
- **Spacers in vstack** — `vstack()` now preserves empty strings, allowing them to function as vertical spacers.
- **EventBus unhandled rejections** — `runCmd()` now catches rejected command promises instead of leaving them unhandled.
- **KeyMap group() safety** — `group()` now uses `try/finally` to restore scope even if the builder callback throws.
- **Duplicate modifier detection** — `parseKeyCombo()` now throws on duplicate modifiers like `"ctrl+ctrl+c"`.

### Showcase

- **High-fidelity demo** — `demo-tui.ts` completely rewritten to demonstrate physics-based springs, GSAP timelines, layered input stacks, real-time process telemetry (CPU/MEM/FPS), and a "Turbo Mode" benchmark.

### Build

- Switched to `tsc -b` with TypeScript project references for dependency-ordered incremental builds
- Added `prepack` script to all packages
- Added `composite: true` to all tsconfig files

## [0.1.0] — 2026-02-25

First public release.

### Added

#### Core (`@flyingrobots/bijou`)

- **Hexagonal architecture** — `RuntimePort`, `IOPort`, `StylePort`, `BijouContext` with automatic output mode detection (interactive, static, pipe, accessible)
- **Layout components** — `box()`, `headerBox()`, `separator()`
- **Element components** — `badge()`, `alert()`, `kbd()`, `skeleton()`
- **Data components** — `table()`, `tree()`, `accordion()`, `timeline()`
- **Navigation components** — `tabs()`, `breadcrumb()`, `stepper()`, `paginator()`
- **Animation** — `spinner()`, `createSpinner()`, `progressBar()`, `createProgressBar()`, `createAnimatedProgressBar()`, `gradientText()`
- **Forms** — `input()`, `select()`, `multiselect()`, `confirm()`, `group()` with validation and graceful pipe/CI degradation
- **Theme engine** — DTCG interop (`fromDTCG`/`toDTCG`), built-in presets (`cyan-magenta`, `nord`, `catppuccin`), `extendTheme()`, `styled()`, `styledStatus()`, `tv()`
- **Test adapters** — `createTestContext()`, `mockRuntime()`, `mockIO()`, `plainStyle()` for deterministic testing without process mocks
- **ASCII logo loader** — `loadRandomLogo()` with small/medium/large sizing

#### Node adapter (`@flyingrobots/bijou-node`)

- `nodeRuntime()`, `nodeIO()`, `chalkStyle()` port implementations
- `createNodeContext()` and `initDefaultContext()` for one-line setup
- Automatic `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`, `CI`, `TERM=dumb` detection

#### TUI runtime (`@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`)

- **TEA (The Elm Architecture) runtime** — `run()` with `App<M>` type (`init`, `update`, `view`)
- **Commands** — `quit()`, `tick()`, `batch()`
- **Key parsing** — `parseKey()` for raw stdin to `KeyMsg`
- **Screen control** — `enterScreen()`, `exitScreen()`, `clearAndHome()`, `renderFrame()`
- **Layout helpers** — `vstack()`, `hstack()`

# Secondary Example Map

This file is no longer a giant per-example status ledger.

It is a maintainer-facing and agent-facing reference map, not a public
docs hub.

DOGFOOD is the primary living-docs and proving surface. In v4.4.0,
31 examples were retired because DOGFOOD now covers their component
families directly. The remaining examples exist for runtime seam
references, shell proving, and leaf API demos that DOGFOOD does not
yet teach.

If you are trying to learn Bijou, start with [DOGFOOD](./DOGFOOD.md),
not this file.

For the full secondary/internal inventory, use
[../examples/README.md](../examples/README.md).

## Keep

These examples still have clear secondary/reference value.

### Runtime References

Keep these as the main runtime reference set for the `v4.0.0` line:

- `examples/v3-demo`
- `examples/v3-css`
- `examples/v3-motion`
- `examples/v3-subapp`
- `examples/v3-worker`
- `examples/v3-pipeline`

They keep the historical `v3-*` names, but they remain the clearest runtime seam references on this branch.

### DOGFOOD And Shell Proving Surfaces

Keep these because they prove product-level behavior rather than isolated leaf rendering:

- `examples/docs`
  - the living docs app and current proving surface
- `examples/release-workbench`
  - canonical multi-view control-room shell
- `examples/notifications`
  - notification stack, routing, history, and shell review behavior
- `examples/app-frame`
  - framed shell reference

### Remaining Leaf Examples

Keep leaf examples when they are the clearest isolated explanation of
a family or API seam not yet covered by DOGFOOD stories. The remaining
set in this file is the current reference for example retirements that
still depend on deeper DOGFOOD teaching. The historical depth follow-on
is [DF-020](./method/retro/DF-020-deepen-dogfood-story-depth-and-variant-quality.md).

## Cut Later

An example becomes a retirement candidate only when all of the following are true:

1. DOGFOOD or another canonical scenario now teaches the same decision clearly.
2. No migration guide or package README still points to the example.
3. It is not carrying unique smoke or regression value.
4. It is not the clearest isolated proof of a public API seam.

## Relationship To Release Smoke

Release smoke now runs through `smoke:dogfood`.

Tracked closure:

- [WF-003 — Replace `smoke:examples:*` With `smoke:dogfood`](./design/WF-003-replace-smoke-examples-with-smoke-dogfood.md)

That means examples are no longer the release-facing smoke contract even
if some internal reference tooling around example scenarios still
exists.

# Bijou documentation

| Surface | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| [Project README](../README.md) | Public front door |
| [Teaching book](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou-job-monitor/blob/main/book/bijou-book.pdf) | Build and test the job monitor |
| [Design Archive](./book/bijou-archive.pdf) | Historical design records |
| [Complete edition](./book/bijou-designs.pdf) | Frozen teaching and historical collection |

[Read the teaching book](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou-job-monitor/blob/main/book/bijou-book.pdf), use the
[Design Archive](./book/bijou-archive.pdf), or
[Read the complete book](./book/bijou-designs.pdf).
See [LaTeX sources and edition details](./book/README.md).

The teaching book follows a job monitor through five Parts: why Bijou, building
the application, understanding its machinery, making it dependable, and shipping
and maintaining it. It includes practical reference material and the component atlas.

The archive preserves 426 guides, principles, design records,
release notes, audits and retrospectives as historical appendices. Their original
claims and status have not been reclassified as current implementation guarantees.
The complete edition preserves the combined 20 October 2026 publication. The live
teaching book and its LaTeX sources now belong to the job-monitor repository.
Individual source Markdown files remain removed;
their exact text and hashes survive in the frozen corpus for DOGFOOD and checks.

Translations: the teaching book (about 13,600 lexical tokens, 106 pages) is
the first edition to be translated. The planned translated sources will live
in the job-monitor repository
under `book/locales/<locale>/`, at the same relative paths as the English files,
and will build to `bijou-book.<locale>.pdf` after locale build support
([#618](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou/issues/618)) lands.
The complete edition and the archive
stay English only, and the English hash pins do not change. See
[DL-036](./design/DL-036-book-translation-edition.md).

For a bounded source excerpt, run from the repository root:

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/read-documentation.ts docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 1 80
```

The arguments are the original path, first line and line limit (maximum 250).
`npm run docs:inventory` lists the retained operating documents and book artifacts.

Start with the teaching book's Preface and version page. Every teaching Part
has an introduction and a concrete learning outcome. The seven workshops use the
separate [published companion repository](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou-job-monitor),
pinned to Bijou 7.2.0 at edition `book-v2`. Five independent build stages, actual
source diffs and an explained exercise answer key support the workshops. The human
walkthrough is prepared; the user will arrange an unfamiliar reader.
The glossary and topic finder support practical lookup.

## Getting started

- [Build your first Bijou app](./guides/getting-started.md): minimal app, packages, layouts, and DOGFOOD controls.
- [Job Monitor tutorial](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou-job-monitor): a complete application and the teaching book.
- [Developing Bijou](./development.md): toolchain, testing, localization, and contribution workflow.
- [Run tests in a disposable Docker copy](./guides/sealed-tests.md): copy-in isolation, offline execution, and validation receipts.

## Current operating references

- [Latest features in DOGFOOD](../examples/docs/content/guides-latest-features.md)
- [MCP package guide](../examples/docs/content/package-mcp.md)
- [Project front door](../README.md)

- [Semantic scene app contract](./topics/semantic-scene-app/README.md): `ui-scene-ir/1` projection, action dispatch, diagnostics, and [test plan](./topics/semantic-scene-app/test-plan.md)

- [Components Library](../examples/components/README.md): every component, one slide at a time, in every output mode
- [DOGFOOD](../examples/docs/README.md): the documentation app, in English, French, Spanish, and German
- [Bijou skill for coding agents](../.claude/skills/bijou/SKILL.md): how to build Bijou apps, choose components, theme, animate, and test

GitHub issues and milestones own current scope. Historical proposals in the book
retain their original status. Linear migration still requires a connected team.

`npm run release:readiness -- --milestone v8.0.0` requires a live release
packet at `docs/releases/8.0.0/stable-acceptance.md` or the legacy `README.md`

Latest Features guide covers later font, typography, animation, and theme work;
the package READMEs and runnable examples provide the detailed current contracts.

Release document paths use the release line: `8.0.0-alpha.1`, `8.0.0-beta.12`,

# Bijou Design System

Bijou now has enough surface area that "here are the exports" is no longer a good documentation strategy.

This section defines the design language behind the library:

- the foundations that shape the UI
- the token vocabulary that turns color doctrine into API rules
- the interaction and layout patterns that recur across apps
- the component families and their intended jobs
- the policy for visualizing data instead of guessing ad hoc each time

This is deliberately closer to a design-system guide than to an API reference.

## What this section is for

Use these docs when you need to answer:

- What problem does this component family solve?
- Which variation should I use?
- Which token family should this component use?
- When should I choose one component over another?
- When should I avoid this component entirely?
- Does this belong in core `@flyingrobots/bijou` or in `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`?
- How should this degrade across interactive, static, pipe, and accessible runs?
- What is the terminal-first equivalent of a desktop/web design-system pattern?

## Read in this order

1. [Foundations](./foundations.md)
2. [Theme Token Vocabulary](./theme-tokens.md)
3. [Theme Authoring Guide](./theme-authoring.md)
4. [Theme Rule Recipes](./theme-rule-recipes.md)
5. [Patterns](./patterns.md)
6. [Blocks](./blocks.md)
7. [Pointer and Mouse Policy](./pointer.md)
8. [Component Families](./component-families.md)
9. [Data Visualization Policy](./data-visualization.md)

For the raw inventory and taxonomy work behind these docs, see [../archive/component-system-audit.md](../archive/component-system-audit.md).

## Core system ideas

### Bijou is not just a component library

Bijou is made of five layers:

1. **Foundations**
  - color, spacing rhythm, text hierarchy, overflow, motion, focus, interruption
2. **Theme vocabulary**
  - canonical token families and first-party usage rules
3. **Patterns**
  - status, selection, browsing, overlays, forms, shell composition
4. **Component families**
  - specific primitives that implement those patterns
5. **Blocks**
  - reusable product-level assemblies such as app frames, settings flows, and guided workflows

Components and blocks should be downstream of the first three layers. If the
design language is weak, the component catalog and block library both become
noisy no matter how many exports exist.

### Core versus TUI ownership

- `@flyingrobots/bijou` owns semantics that survive degradation.
- `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` owns focus, motion, overlays, shell behavior, scrolling, history, and other lifecycle-heavy interactions.

That means:

- `alert()` belongs in core.
- `toast()` belongs in TUI.
- notifications belong in TUI because they are a system, not just a rendering.

### Variations are not all equal

Bijou uses three kinds of variation:

- **semantic variants**
  - for example status tone or severity
- **interaction-layer variants**
  - for example `accordion()` versus `interactiveAccordion()`
- **render-path variants**
  - for example `box()` versus `boxSurface()`

Only the first kind is a "visual variant" in the usual design-system sense. The other two exist because Bijou has to survive different interaction and rendering layers.

### Graceful lowering is a first-class design constraint

Every family should answer:

- What does this look like in a rich interactive terminal?
- What remains true in static CI output?
- What remains true in pipe mode?
- What becomes simpler in accessible mode?

If a component cannot answer that question, it probably belongs in `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui`, not in core.

## Documentation standard

Every mature component-family page in Bijou should include:

- What it is
- Variations
- When to use
- When not to use
- Content guidance
- Interaction ownership
- Graceful lowering path
- Related families

The component-family guide now meets this structural baseline and its structure is checked by a repo preflight script. That preflight is intentionally structural: it verifies required family sections and graceful-lowering mode coverage inside the family guide. Semantic accuracy, package/example doc drift, and touched-component doc completeness are still review responsibilities, not something the current script can prove automatically.

## Component-change gate

From the v4 pure-surface cleanup onward, any component-family change should be evaluated against the docs in the same slice.

For every component or component family touched, verify:

- documentation exists
- documented variants are current
- `When to use` guidance is present and still accurate
- `When not to use` guidance is present and still accurate
- core-versus-TUI ownership is explicit
- graceful lowering is documented across `rich`, `static`, `pipe`, and `accessible` when applicable
- related families are listed

The CI preflight enforces the structural minimum for the family guide. If any of the broader checks below are missing or materially wrong, the docs are still incomplete and that gap should be fixed in the same slice or explicitly logged as backlog debt before the work is considered done.

## Current gaps this section is meant to close

Bijou is already strong on breadth and runtime architecture. The weaker parts are:

- explicit usage guidance
- family-level documentation
- documentation completeness against the standard defined above
- pattern-level decision support
- data-visualization doctrine
- mouse and multi-input policy

These docs exist to correct that.
